issues.legal_issue: The statutory bar on court proceedings for eviction from vacant land does not apply to a proceeding between private persons to determine possession and prevent a breach of the peace.
material_facts: A proceeding was initiated under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure after one private party alleged that another had forcibly dispossessed him from a hotel on disputed land.
The land was vacant land in an urban area covered by the Maharashtra Vacant Lands Act, and that Act came into force while the proceeding was pending.
The proceeding concerned competing claims to possession between private persons, not eviction by the competent authority under the Act.
issues.conclusion: The bar in section 8 of the Act did not apply, the proceeding did not abate, and the Magistrate retained jurisdiction to dispose of it under sections 145 and 146 of the Code.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8 of the Maharashtra Vacant Lands (Prohibition of Unauthorised Occupation and Summary Eviction) Act, 1975 bars proceedings concerning eviction by the competent authority under section 4, including proceedings that the authority is entitled to bring against a person in unauthorised occupation. It does not bar a proceeding between private persons claiming authorised possession, where the competent authority is not involved. A proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is primarily directed at preventing a breach of the peace by determining who is entitled to remain in possession until eviction in due course of law. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.private_possession_proceeding: A proceeding was brought to determine possession of land between private persons and prevent a breach of the peace.
predicates.competing_private_claims: The private parties each claimed a right to possess the disputed land.
predicates.authority_not_seeking_eviction: The competent public authority was not seeking to evict a person from the land.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns competing private claims to possession and no competent authority is seeking eviction, the proceeding is not barred or abated.

issues.legal_issue: Restoring a party who was forcibly and wrongfully dispossessed within the statutory period is a means of determining that party’s deemed possession, not an eviction proceeding under the vacant-lands statute.
material_facts: The complainant alleged that he had been forcibly dispossessed shortly before initiating the possession proceeding.

The proceeding was brought under section 145, whose proviso allows a Magistrate to treat a party forcibly and wrongfully dispossessed within the specified period as having been in possession on the date of the preliminary order.
The statutory treatment of the dispossessed party as being in possession could require the opposing party to be physically removed from the property.
issues.conclusion: Any physical removal required to give effect to the statutory fiction is only for treating the dispossessed party as being in possession on the relevant date; it does not turn the proceeding into an eviction proceeding barred by the Act.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to section 145(4) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 permits the Magistrate, where a party was forcibly and wrongfully dispossessed within the prescribed period, to treat that party as being in possession on the date of the preliminary order; section 145(6)(a) gives effect to that treatment. Any physical restoration is for determining possession under that legal fiction. The proceeding remains directed to preventing a breach of the peace, not to eviction under sections 4 and 8 of the Maharashtra Vacant Lands Act. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.private_possession_proceeding: A proceeding was brought between private persons to determine possession and prevent a breach of the peace.
predicates.forcible_wrongful_dispossession_within_q: A party was forcibly and wrongfully dispossessed within the period relevant to the proceeding.
predicates.dispossessed_party_treated_as_in_possess: The Magistrate treats the dispossessed party as having been in possession on the date used to decide possession.

issues.definition: When a party is treated as having been in possession after qualifying forcible and wrongful dispossession in a private possession proceeding, restoration serves that deemed-possession determination rather than a statutory eviction.

issues.legal_issue: In a possession proceeding involving attached property, the Magistrate must determine possession where possible and otherwise maintain attachment until a competent court determines the parties’ rights.
material_facts: The Magistrate had attached the disputed property during the proceeding.
The Supreme Court remitted the proceeding for disposal under sections 145 and 146 of the Code.
The Magistrate could determine that one party was in possession, or could find that neither party was in possession or be unable to determine which party was in possession.
issues.conclusion: The Magistrate must determine possession if able; if a party is declared in possession, the other party must be prevented from disturbing that possession and the attachment must be withdrawn. If neither party was in possession or the Magistrate cannot determine possession, the attachment may remain until a competent court determines the parties’ rights.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the Magistrate should determine possession from the evidence and declare the party found in possession, including deemed possession where the proviso to section 145(4) applies. Under the proviso to section 146(1), the attachment is to be withdrawn when a party is declared in possession and the likelihood of a breach of the peace is thereby removed. If neither party was in possession, or the Magistrate cannot determine possession, section 146(1) permits the attachment to continue until a competent court determines the rights of the parties; section 146(2) may be used where necessary. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.possession_proceeding_with_attached_prop: A Magistrate is deciding a proceeding to prevent a breach of the peace over land and the disputed property has been attached.

issues.definition: When disputed property is attached in a possession proceeding, the Magistrate must determine possession where possible and handle the attachment according to that determination.
